results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

### The second increase this year

This is not the first increase. The Motley Fool reports that in early May, Nebius's pricing page showed H100 at $2.95 per hour and B300 at $6.10. [2] Our own catalog recorded H100 at $3.85 on September 18 and B300 at $7.85 on September 24.

If the May figures are right, the October rates are about 53% higher for H100 and 56% higher for B300 than five months earlier. [2] The trend matters more than any single rate. A budget built on spring pricing may already be out of date.

### How the new rates compare

We compared the new rates with published on demand rates in our provider catalog, checked September 18 to 28.

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.

If you are planning a project, get a dated quote for your actual start date. Ask what a 3, 6 or 12 month commitment costs against the new on demand rate. Ask whether that commitment reserves GPUs or only lowers the rate.

results.title: AI Rental Rates Rise, Hyperscale Loses Default Status, and Sovereign AI Moves Upstack · Cloud Computing | Drip
highlights:
## Nebius, Oracle, and Vessl AI Push AI Rental Rates Higher as Delivery Tightens

Nebius raised selected Nvidia GPU rates 17%–21%, Oracle renewed expiring GPU contracts about 20% higher, and Vessl AI lifted H100 pricing in Korea by 24.7%, where local H100 rentals were up 21.9% month over month to $3.28. This week’s change is less about another broad market repricing than about operators passing through the cost of turning already-contracted chips into usable capacity as cooling, power, and facility constraints tighten.

The repricing is segmented, not uniform. Oracle is resetting expiring contracts, Nebius is targeting specific SKUs, and Korea is seeing the steepest move, showing that scarcity is being monetized where deliverability is tightest. Utility interconnection delays measured in years, difficulty securing hundreds of megawatts, and the shift beyond air cooling at roughly 50–100 kW per rack are turning deployment timelines and retrofit complexity into billable constraints. Liquid cooling and dry-cooler designs ease density limits but raise capex, especially in retrofits.

For operators, pricing power now depends on control of power, cooling, and site readiness, not just GPU access. For vendors and investors, the progression from contracted capacity to delivered throughput keeps shifting value toward thermal, electrical, and development capabilities that shorten the path to revenue.

results.title: Nebius's Oct. 1 Price Hike: The 41% Memory Jump Is the Real Signal | AInvest
highlights:
- Nebius NBIS-- raised GPU/memory prices 17-41% amid AI compute scarcity, with memory surging twice as fast due to HBM/DRAM supply constraints.

...

A cloud company raising prices usually reads as margin-grabbing. When AI-cloud provider Nebius NBIS-- (NBIS) told customers on Sept. 17 that pay-as-you-go rates on its Nvidia NVDA-- GPUs would climb 17% to 21% starting Oct. 1, the stock rose on the news rather than fell. The market smelled scarcity, not greed, and that is the right read - but only half of it. The line in the notice that says the most is the roughly 41% increase on memory, and understanding why memory went up twice as fast as the chips tells you where this AI compute cycle is actually binding.

Start with what a price hike means in a cloud business. Renting out Nvidia chips is a supply-constrained game: when demand outstrips the fleet a provider can stand up, the scarce few raise list prices - the same fingerprint as the 2023 H100 shortage. Nebius made its on-demand rates 17% to 21% higher on selected GPUs, raised some CPU-only instances by 25%, and lifted memory about 41%. It was the company's second price rise in a matter of months, and it is not a Nebius quirk: competitor CoreWeave reportedly signed contracts at higher prices the same day. When the whole rental market reprices up together, that is demand, not one operator testing its pricing power.

Now the detail that carries the story. The percentages are not uniform because the scarcity is not uniform. Per GPU-hour, the H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 and the H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, while the newest Blackwell parts rose the most - the B200 to $8.50 and the B300 to $9.50. Memory was the outlier at roughly 41%. The newest chips are the binding reason: each B300 carries more high-bandwidth memory per chip than its predecessors, and HBM and DRAM fabrication capacity is being fought over against the phone and PC makers at Samsung, SK Hynix SKHY--, and Micron MU--. So the constraint has moved down the stack. A price list that shows memory inflating about twice as fast as the GPUs that consume it is a live reading that the bottleneck has shifted from GPU dies to the memory under them - information an investor can catch in a vendor notice before it shows up evenly across earnings.

results.title: Nebius will raise hourly GPU prices by up to 21% on Oct. 1 · Infive
highlights:
Nebius will raise on-demand rates for four Nvidia GPU models by 17% to 21% on Oct. 1, including B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 an hour. CFO Dado Alonso said in August that capacity sold out as fast as it came online; existing contracts won't be repriced.

The increases cover H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPUs, plus CPU-only servers. Nebius listed the H100 at $2.95 an hour and the B300 at $6.10 in early May; after the new rates, they will cost $4.50 and $9.50—about 53% and 56% more, respectively.

Nebius does not disclose how much revenue comes from hourly rentals versus reserved-capacity contracts. At June's end, it reported $37.5 billion in remaining performance obligations—signed revenue not yet recognized—more than 60 times its $582 million second-quarter revenue. The Oct. 1 increase won't reprice that backlog and mainly signals rates for capacity not yet sold; the article warns prices could fall if supply catches up.

results.title: Nebius Raises AI Compute Prices as Data Center Power Limits Tighten - WalletInvestor.com
highlights:
A cloud provider in the middle of an aggressive build-out just told its customers it will charge them more, not less, to rent GPUs. Nebius, the AI infrastructure company spun out of the old Yandex, is raising the price of its compute on October 1. In a market where scale is supposed to drive costs down, a supplier moving the other way is worth reading closely, because it says something plain about how tight the supply of AI compute still is.

## Nebius lifts GPU rental rates on October 1

The intuition most investors carry is that renting a chip by the hour should get cheaper as more capacity comes online. More data centers, more GPUs, more competition, lower prices. That’s how commodity compute usually behaves. Nebius is doing the opposite, and the reason is straightforward: demand for high-end accelerators is running ahead of the industry’s ability to install them. When a provider can sell every hour of capacity it has and still turn customers away, a discount makes no sense. Raising the rate is the rational move, and it’s also the honest signal — a company confident it can fill its racks at a higher price is telling you the shortage hasn’t eased.

This matters beyond one mid-sized cloud. The companies renting compute are the same startups and enterprises trying to train and serve AI models, and their input cost just went up. Every price increase at the infrastructure layer flows through to the economics of the applications built on top. If compute stays expensive, the pressure to justify AI spending with real revenue gets heavier, not lighter.

...

Underneath the compute crunch sits a harder constraint that doesn’t clear as quickly as a chip order: electricity. ... Developers file interconnection requests for enormous loads — hundreds of megawatts, sometimes more than a gigawatt — to lock in a spot in the

...

The result is a queue clogged with phantom demand. Utilities can’t tell how much of the requested load is real, which makes it hard to plan generation and transmission, which in turn slows the projects that are real. Power availability, grid interconnection timelines, and the multi-year lead times on transformers and turbines are now the gating factor on how fast AI capacity can grow. A company can order all the GPUs it wants; if it can’t get power to the building, the chips sit in a warehouse.

That’s the reconciliation between the two stories. Nebius can raise prices precisely because the physical build-out — power first, then buildings, then installed silicon — can’t keep pace with demand. Scarcity at the plug shows up as scarcity at the price.

results.title: How GPU Prices Can Double While AI Gets Cheaper • Tomasz Tunguz
highlights:
In short : GPU rental prices doubled in six months while inference prices kept falling. The reconciliation is efficiency : the hinge that turns scarce silicon into cheap intelligence.

GPU prices have doubled in the last six months, from $4.40 to $8.08 per GPU-hour. But AI prices are falling. How can that be?

It is not a simple answer. Higher GPU costs are likely to remain while the industry races to build out new data centers. Every component of the buildout is increasing in cost, from concrete to copper to credit. 1 Above all, electricity remains the limiting factor, which Oracle is experiencing : last week it invoked force majeure on its New Mexico campus after the natural-gas pipeline feeding it slipped by six months. 2 

Demand continues to explode. Inference companies & model companies are posting record-setting growth, which emboldens investors to value them more richly, provide them more capital, & up the bidding on those limited GPU-hours, to generate more revenue. The flywheel spins.

results.title: 10月算力将大爆发！连临时租卡都租不到，Nebius第二轮涨价21%？_腾讯新闻
highlights:
10月1日起， Nebius把 B300的GPU时租价从7.85美元提到9.5美元，涨幅21%。这是它今年第二轮涨价，而且这次涨的是按需现货市场。就在半年前，同样这卡的价格还是6.1美元，半年涨了超过一半。算力这东西，正从"想租就能租"变成"出价也得排队"。

Nebius是家荷兰的AI算力租赁商，客户里有Meta和微软，英伟达在7月披露持有它大约9.3%的股权。它这次不是单独涨哪一款，而是全系上抬。 H100从3.85美元涨到4.5美元，涨17%； H200从4.5美元到5.4美元，涨20%； B200从7.15美元到8.5美元，涨近19%；B300最高，21%。连配套的CPU和内存也没落下， AMD EPYC Genoa的CPU费率上调25%，内存费率上调约41%。

最值得留意的是涨价范围。今年5月那轮调价，主要动的是长期合约客户，相当于大客户愿意提前把钱锁进来。这一轮直接落到现货、临时按需租赁市场，说明短期的临时算力需求，供给也已经跟不上了。云厂商心里最清楚自己手里有多少货，肯给现货涨价，往往是实在腾不出余量。

这批上涨里，2022年发布的H100也跟着涨了17%。按很多人原来的说法，GPU过两三年就该淘汰折旧，可这台服役四年的老卡租金不降反升，反倒说明需求端对算力是真缺，而不是挑挑拣拣。Nebius的管理层说得更直白，按现在的合约条款，2027年的产能今天就能全部卖完。

算力紧缺不是一家的事。另一家同样获英伟达注资的 CoreWeave早在7月就全系提价约25%，并表示第三季度价格还在往上走。两家头部租赁商同步抬价，背后的原因一致，AI推理和智能体业务在持续消耗算力，而高端芯片产能在短期放不出来，供给的速度追不上需求的增长。

需求端的数字也在解释这轮涨价为什么能持续。上半年英伟达H100的一年期租赁合约价，从2025年10月的1.7美元一路涨到2026年3月的2.35美元，涨幅接近40%。国内这边，头部云厂商此前已多次上调AI算力相关服务价格，阿里云在4月的一周内就连续宣布过三轮调价。算力租赁的定价逻辑，正在从早先靠"谁能拿到卡"的签约阶段，转向"客户愿不愿意为算力付更多钱"的验证阶段。

...

把单家厂商的涨价当成行业永久不变的规律，也容易踩坑。这轮价格上行的前提，是供给扩张跑不赢需求。可一旦芯片供给放量，或者下游AI需求的增速慢下来，当前的价格逻辑就会松动。涨价不会无休止地持续下去。
